$description: What each component's Figma node must say about itself. Generated from the contracts and src/tokens/figma-map.js by scripts/build-figma-docs.ts — edit those, not this file.
rules: **One solid `Action` per view.** It is the next step. Everything else is `neutral`, `ghost` or, over imagery, `glass`.

**Tokens only.** Colours, radii, shadows and curves come from the Tailwind preset (`bg-surface-card`, `text-cream`, `text-cream-dim`, `border-line`, `bg-accent`, `rounded-card`, `shadow-lift`, `ease-press`, `text-title`). No hex, no `rgb()`, no arbitrary values for anything a token covers. Never red: nothing in this product marks a person wrong.

**No app imports.** Nothing from `@/…`, nothing from `../web`, no `useT`, `useLocale` or `useThesisT`. Imports inside the package are relative (`../Action`). Default strings are props with Spanish defaults.

**Contracts stay true.** Change the code and you change the contract, the previews and the guidance in the same edit. A new or removed prop or state means a `version` bump and a `changelog` entry (major for breaking, minor for additions, patch for fixes); the newest changelog entry equals `version`.

**Real copy.** Spanish first, tú (never vos or usted, outside the simulated jury), sentence case, actions start with a verb, no exclamation marks, gender-neutral, calm. Example copy is quoted from the product (`web/src/lib/thesis-copy.ts`, `web/src/lib/i18n.ts`), never invented: "Ensayar mi sustentación", "Sube tu tesis", "Ver planes", "Ahora no".

**Generated files are generated.** Do not edit `src/tokens/tokens.json`, `src/tokens/theme.css`, `src/tokens/figma.json` or `registry.json`. Edit `src/tokens/tokens.css`, the preset or `src/tokens/figma-map.js` and run `npm run tokens`; change components and run `npm run registry`.
**Run `npm run check` before you finish.** It checks generated files, types, contracts, previews (rendered and run through axe) and tokens. Do not report work as done while it fails.

**Nothing with a redistribution-restricted licence** (React Bits and similar). The registry hands these files to other tools. Code comments, contract descriptions and Markdown guidance are in English. Strings a person reads are in Spanish.

components.name: Action
components.description:
The button. One primary per view, in the accent; everything else steps down in tone.

**Use it for:** Any action the user takes on purpose: start, save, send, confirm, open a flow; The single most important next step of a screen (tone solid, often withArrow).

**Not for:** Navigating to another page as plain navigation → A link (<a> / router Link) styled as a link; wrap an Action in a Link only when the destination is a step forward; Choosing one option among several → Segmented (2–5 options) or a radio group.

**Also known as:** button, botón, CTA, call to action, primary button, secondary button, ghost button, link button.

`import { Action } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: One solid Action per view; demote the rest to neutral or ghost.
Put the primary on the right of a pair on desktop and first in the stack on mobile.
Explain a disabled Action in text next to it.
dont: Don't put two solid Actions side by side — the user has to read both to know which matters.
Don't restyle the tone with className colours; add a tone to the contract instead.
Don't use withArrow on secondary or destructive actions.

components.name: Badge
components.description:
A small pill with a status in words — the mode of a call, a setting in force — and, when live, a breathing dot.

**Use it for:** A short fact about the current screen that the user is not changing right now: the mode of a call, a setting in force; A status happening at this moment, with tone live: the call connecting, the interviewer's turn.

**Not for:** Something the user can press or toggle → Action (ghost) or Segmented. A Badge is not focusable and has no press; Marking an option as part of the paid plan → PremiumMark.

**Also known as:** tag, chip, pill, status, estado, etiqueta, live indicator.

`import { Badge } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Say the state in words; let the dot only add "right now".
One live badge per view at most.
Add role="status" when the text changes in place.
dont: Don't use a Badge as a button or a filter chip.
Don't make every badge live.
Don't recolour it to mean error or success.

components.name: CheckItem
components.description:
One row of a checklist of what a plan or an offer includes: a check in the accent, then the words.

**Use it for:** Listing what a plan or an offer includes: the pricing cards, the early-access offer; A short list of things the reader gets, where every row is a yes.

**Not for:** Something the user ticks or unticks → Checkbox; Steps to follow in order → An ordered list (<ol>) with numbers; a check says done or included, not next.

**Also known as:** checklist item, feature list item, benefit row, bullet, ítem con check, lista de beneficios.

`import { CheckItem } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Put it inside a <ul> with a label before it, such as "Qué incluye".
Keep rows of one list to the same shape and length.
Lay rows out with flex-col gap-3 on the list.
dont: Don't render a CheckItem outside a list.
Don't use a check for something that is not included.
Don't recolour the check to rank rows.

components.name: Eyebrow
components.description:
The short line in the accent above a heading or a value: it says where the reader is, the heading says what it means.

**Use it for:** Above a landing section's heading, to place it: "Precios", "Acceso anticipado"; Above a value in a platform card: "Nivel" over the level, "Acta simulada" over the grade.

**Not for:** The name of a section or a page → A heading (an h2 inside Section, the title of PageHeader). The eyebrow goes above it, never in place of it; A status or a mode on an item → Badge.

**Also known as:** kicker, overline, pre-title, section label, antetítulo.

`import { Eyebrow } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Pair it with a heading that says something.
One eyebrow per block.
Use className for spacing and grid placement only.
dont: Don't make it the only title of a section.
Don't set it in spaced capitals or another colour.
Don't end it with a period or a colon.

components.name: Panel
components.description:
The surface every card, block and sheet sits on: a rounded fill with the card shadow, or glass over imagery. No padding, no states.

**Use it for:** Any block of content that belongs together on a page: a step, a form section, an empty state, a wait, a tier; A grid of equal items: give them all variant="card" and h-full so the row lines up.

**Not for:** A card the person presses as a whole (a session row, a nav tile) → A link or button styled with the card tokens itself (focus-ring rounded-2xl bg-surface-card shadow-card hover:shadow-lift), as RecentSessions does. Panel has no hover, focus or pressed state; A group inside a panel → An inset well: rounded-2xl bg-surface-lift p-4. A Panel inside a Panel doubles the edge and the radius.

**Also known as:** card, tarjeta, surface, container, box, sheet, tile.

`import { Panel } from "@mockio/design-system";`

slot.Content: Whatever the card holds, padded by its own content (the Panel adds none). Usually an Eyebrow, a title in Title, CheckItems and one row of Actions.

do: Use card for siblings in a grid and raised for a single block on the page.
Give the panel its padding through className: p-6 sm:p-8.
Give a wait role="status" and a failure role="alert".
Mark the recommended one of a set with ring-2 ring-accent, not a glow.
dont: Don't put hover:shadow-lift on a panel nothing happens on — it promises a press.
Don't nest a Panel in a Panel.
Don't recolour it with bg-* or border-*; pick the variant.
Don't reach for glass on a plain page for a grid of ordinary cards: on the dark theme it is near-transparent and reads as empty; use card.

components.name: PremiumMark
components.description:
The gold crown on an option that belongs to the paid plan, named for screen readers; the option itself stays usable.

**Use it for:** Next to any option the free plan cannot use: a rail entry, a practice tab, a share template, a section of the report; Wherever the option appears, the same mark — so it is learnt once.

**Not for:** Saying the paid plan is active for this person → ShimmerText in the top bar's "Premium" chip; A status of the current screen → Badge.

**Also known as:** premium badge, crown, pro badge, paid indicator, corona, insignia premium.

`import { PremiumMark } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Keep the marked option visible and pressable; let the press explain or open the plans.
Put it at the end of the option's label (ms-auto in a full-width row).
Use the default label unless the place needs "Del plan pago".
dont: Don't disable an option because it carries the mark.
Don't use the crown or the gold for anything else.
Don't resize or recolour it through className.

components.name: PageHeader
components.description:
The title block of every app screen: the page's only h1, one line of meta and the screen's actions, on the same container as PageBody.

**Use it for:** At the top of every screen in the signed-in app, once, directly above its PageBody; compact for a screen whose content needs the height on a phone: the live call.

**Not for:** A marketing page's headline → The hero's own h1, then Sections with h2; A heading inside the screen → An h2 in a Panel.

**Also known as:** page title, screen header, title bar, h1, encabezado de página.

`import { PageHeader } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Pass the same width to PageHeader and PageBody.
Put the point of the meta in its first 35 characters: that is what a 320px phone shows.
Keep one Action in actions, and make it solid only when it is the screen's way forward.
dont: Don't render a second PageHeader (or any other h1) on a screen.
Don't put something the person must read to act in meta: on touch, the clamped part cannot be revealed.
Don't draw a rule or a background under the header.

components.name: Mascot
components.description:
Mocki, the parrot of the interview product, in one of six illustrated growth stages — from egg to crowned.

**Use it for:** The interview product's gamified layer: progress, a level-up, the habit section of the landing; A first-run moment in the interview space, where a face lowers the stakes (the welcome checklist).

**Not for:** Any screen of Sustentación, the thesis space: its landing, upload, diagnosis, rehearsal, acta and plan → No character. The thesis space speaks as a calm person beside the student, not a mascot; use Mark or Wordmark for the brand, and plain copy in a Panel or a Notice for empty and error states; The brand logo, in a header, a favicon or a footer → Mark (the reduced isologo) or Wordmark (the lockup with the name).

**Also known as:** Mocki, avatar, character, mascota, loro, parrot, level avatar.

`import { Mascot } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Pass decorative when a heading or a message beside it already says what is happening.
Pass a translated alt for every locale other than Spanish.
Keep it at 100px or less where it must look sharp; it is a 200px master.
dont: Don't use Mocki in Sustentación, or as the logo.
Don't recolour, crop or flip it; it carries its own colour.
Don't pair it with exclamation marks or anglicisms ("¡Mocki evolucionó! Mira su nuevo look." is the product string to fix, not to copy).

components.name: Mark
components.description:
The isologo: Mocki the parrot as three shapes on the mustard tile, in the brand's fixed colours, legible down to 16px.

**Use it for:** The product's corner of the app shell, beside or instead of the written name (the top bar at 30px); Any place the brand must be recognisable in a square: an icon tile, a compact header.

**Not for:** The brand needs to be read, not only recognised (landing nav, footer, sign-in) → Wordmark — the mark and the name as one lockup; Showing the user's progress or a friendly face in an empty state, an error or a level-up → Mascot — the full illustrated Mocki, in one of its six stages.

**Also known as:** logo, isologo, app icon, favicon, logotipo.

`import { Mark } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Leave it decorative when the name is written next to it, and name the link instead.
Give the tile's corner to the shadow with a matching rounded class when you add shadow-card.
Keep it at 16px or larger: it is drawn to read at favicon size and no smaller.
dont: Don't recolour it with className, filters or currentColor: the colours are the brand.
Don't rotate, stretch, outline or mirror it, in any direction or locale.
Don't put text on top of it or crop the tile.

components.name: Wordmark
components.description:
The brand lockup: the Mark and the lowercase name "mockio", sized together by font-size so the logo never drifts between places.

**Use it for:** Where the brand is read, not only recognised: the landing nav, the site footer, the sign-in and unsubscribe pages; Beside the Mark in the app's top bar on wide screens, with mark={false}.

**Not for:** A square place or a tight space where the name will not fit (phone top bar, icon tile) → Mark alone, inside a link named "Mockio"; The brand inside a sentence → Plain text "Mockio", capitalised, in the sentence's own font.

**Also known as:** logo, lockup, brand, logotype, marca, logotipo con nombre.

`import { Wordmark } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Size it with a text-* class and let the mark follow.
Use mark={false} when a Mark or a Mascot is already next to it.
Name the home link once (aria-label on the link) and keep the lockup inside it.
dont: Don't build the lockup by hand with a Mark and a text node: the size relation and the lowercase drift.
Don't capitalise it, translate it or route it through a translation function.
Don't add a tagline or a second word inside the lockup.

components.name: Field
components.description:
A form control with its label above and an optional hint below, at the spacing every form in the product shares.

**Use it for:** Any form control that needs a visible label: sign-in, reset password, settings, the early-access form; A setting in a settings grid whose effect needs a sentence of explanation, in the hint.

**Not for:** A message about what just happened after submitting → Notice, below the fields and above the Action; A heading over a group of fields or a block → Eyebrow, then the Fields under it.

**Also known as:** input, text field, form field, select, textarea, campo, campo de formulario.

`import { Field } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Always pass htmlFor and the matching id on a native control.
Give the control the field-control class so it matches every other field.
Put the rule a value must meet in the hint, before the person types, and wire it with hintId.
dont: Don't use the placeholder as the label: it disappears as soon as someone types.
Don't put an error in the hint; the outcome of a submit is a Notice.
Don't draw a box or border around the Field; the control's well is the field.

components.name: Notice
components.description:
A message about what just happened, in a tinted box with its mark: it did not work and what to do next, it worked, or something neutral.

**Use it for:** The outcome of a form submit: under the fields, above the Action (sign in, reset password); The result of a request the page made on its own (confirming an email, unsubscribing).

**Not for:** A rule a value must meet, before anyone types → Field's hint; A standing fact about the screen, such as its mode → Badge.

**Also known as:** alert, banner, callout, message, aviso, mensaje, toast inline.

`import { Notice } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Say what happened and what to do next, in that order.
One Notice per outcome, placed where the person was looking when they acted.
Use tone error for anything that did not work; it is orange, never red.
dont: Don't use a Notice for instructions that were true before anything happened.
Don't stack several Notices; merge them into one message.
Don't recolour it red or add a second icon.

components.name: Segmented
components.description:
A pill of two to five options where exactly one is chosen, with a thumb that slides to the choice. A radio group to assistive technology.

**Use it for:** Choosing one of two to five mutually exclusive options whose effect is immediate: the theme, a filter on a list, the length of the exposition; Switching between two or three views of the same content in place, such as the study sheet and the cards.

**Not for:** Six or more options, or options that need a sentence each → A radio list (stacked radios with descriptions) or a select; Moving between sections of a page that each have their own panel and heading → A tablist (role="tab" + tabpanel), as the settings screen does.

**Also known as:** segmented control, tabs, toggle group, radio group, pestañas, selector.

`import { Segmented } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Keep the labels short and parallel so the slots stay narrow.
Pass a label that matches the visible field name next to it.
Apply the choice at once; a Segmented never needs a Save.
dont: Don't put actions in it: each option is a value, not a command.
Don't use it for more than five options or for long labels — it gets wider than a phone.
Don't recolour the thumb to mark one option as right or recommended.

components.name: DisclosureMark
components.description:
The pill at the end of a <details> summary that says the card opens — a chevron that turns over when open and, on larger disclosures, the word for what clicking does.

**Use it for:** At the end of a <summary> drawn as a card or a row, so it reads as something that opens: "La conversación", "Ver el detalle completo"; With a label on the larger disclosures, where the summary is a title and a line of body: "Tu plan hasta el día D" with "Ver"/"Cerrar", the plans with "Ver planes"/"Ocultar".

**Not for:** A button that opens a menu, a sheet or a dialog → Action (ghost or neutral) with its own words; the mark only follows a <details>; A card that navigates somewhere → A link, with Action's arrow if it needs a sign. A chevron down promises the content opens in place.

**Also known as:** chevron, expand, accordion toggle, disclosure, ver más, desplegable.

`import { DisclosureMark } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Put it inside a <summary>, last, with the summary's text before it.
Give the summary list-none, focus-ring and cursor-pointer, so it looks and behaves like the product's disclosures.
Use a label only where the summary is a title and a line of body.
dont: Don't put it on a button or a link: outside <summary> it never turns and its words never swap.
Don't use it to promise content that loads on a new screen.
Don't repeat the summary's text in the label.

components.name: Meter
components.description:
A measured amount on a known scale — a score out of ten, a percentage, the XP into a level — as a label, the number and a bar that fills to it.

**Use it for:** A score on a fixed scale in a report: vocabulary and structure out of ten in the feedback detail; How far into a level someone is: XP into the next level on the progress screen.

**Not for:** Something loading or being evaluated, with no real total → A sentence that names what is happening ("Evaluando…"); A status in words, not a quantity → Badge.

**Also known as:** progress bar, gauge, score bar, barra de progreso, medidor.

`import { Meter } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Pass the suffix that matches the scale: "/10" with max 10, "" for XP.
Put related meters in one grid or column so the bars compare.
Say in words, near the meters, what the scores mean for the next step.
dont: Don't use a Meter as a loading bar.
Don't recolour the fill to mark a low score: nothing in this product marks a person wrong.
Don't show a meter without its number by hiding it with className.

components.name: MonoLabel
components.description:
The "::LABEL" that names a card or a section in the instrument voice — mono, spaced caps, cream-dim, led by two colons.

**Use it for:** The name of a card on the landing's instrument look: a pricing tier ("Pack Sustentación"), a widget; A section's kicker above its title on the landing: "Cómo funciona" over "De tu PDF a tu acta en una tarde.".

**Not for:** The line above a heading inside the signed-in product → Eyebrow, the product's kicker in the accent; The name of the block in a screen reader's heading list → A heading (h2/h3) under the label. The label is a paragraph.

**Also known as:** card label, overline, instrument label, caption, etiqueta mono, ::LABEL.

`import { MonoLabel } from "@mockio/design-system";`
do: Write the label in sentence case and let the style uppercase it.
Keep a real heading under a section label.
One label per card, at its top.
dont: Don't type the colons: the component draws them.
Don't write a sentence in spaced caps.
Don't use it inside the signed-in product, where the kicker is Eyebrow.
